tasks.title: HANGS General Contracting · Q3 2026 Quarterly Review
tasks.description: Review HANGS General Contracting LP's quarter ended September 30, 2026 for the bonding company and the lender from 8 Excel, PDF and Word files: the comparative trial balance, the interim statements and budget, the controller's written answers, the job schedule, the Q3 payroll ledger and the bank's loan statement and covenants. Inquiry and analytical procedures, not an audit: compare the quarter, investigate every change over the threshold, corroborate each answer, rebuild revenue from the jobs, set expectations for wages and interest and recompute the loan covenants. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft review memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine expresses no conclusion.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft review memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and memo, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Review procedures, not an audit. Not a review report and no conclusion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.

lines.text: At June 30 margins the quarter’s jobs would have earned $2,180,047.50 of gross profit; they earned $1,797,327.50. One job explains it: Tideflats Cold Storage earned $82,800.00 on $4,048,000.00 of revenue, $382,720.00 below its June margin, because its estimate rose from $16,284,000.00 to $17,480,000.00 and the whole year-to-date effect lands in this quarter. lines.text: From the balances, the rates and actual/360 days the quarter’s interest should be $98,140.50; the books show $91,455.50. The books’ figure is exactly what the bank debited on July 1, August 1 and September 1, the interest for June, July and August: interest is recorded when paid. September’s $35,350.00, on the bank’s own statement, is not accrued (accrued interest in the books: $0.00), and June’s $28,665.00 landed in this quarter. Expense is understated $6,685.00 and liabilities $35,350.00 (INT-01). This contradicts Q5, which says interest is accrued monthly (INQ-01).

lines.text: Working capital $4,789,499.00 (minimum $3,000,000) and total liabilities to tangible net worth 2.46 to 1 (maximum 2.75) are met. Tangible net worth must leave out everything due from affiliates: Juniper Ridge Partners’ $571,000.00 receivable, $94,000.00 retainage and $50,500.00 underbilled, $715,500.00 in all. That leaves $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum. Record INT-01 and leave out PCO-14 and it falls to $6,335,449.00, $164,551.00 short: the covenant, and whether the loans stay long-term, turn on the CPA’s judgment on PCO-14 (COV-01).
